questions.q: What does demand mean in economics?
options: The amount people would like to have
The quantity consumers are willing and able to buy at a given price
The quantity firms want to sell
The amount a shop has in stock
questions.why: Demand needs both willingness and ability to pay.

questions.q: A rise in the price of a good causes:
options: A shift of its demand curve to the left
A contraction along its demand curve
A shift of its demand curve to the right
An extension along its demand curve
questions.why: A change in the good's own price is a movement along the curve. A rise in price is a contraction.

questions.q: Incomes rise. What is likely to happen to the demand curve for foreign holidays?
options: It shifts right
It shifts left
A contraction along it
No change
questions.why: Foreign holidays are a normal good, so more are demanded at every price.

questions.q: The price of games consoles falls sharply. What is the likely effect on the demand curve for console games?
options: It shifts right
It shifts left
No effect
An extension along it
questions.why: They are complements. More consoles sold means more games demanded at every price.

questions.q: A news report that a food is unhealthy would shift its demand curve to the left.
questions.why: A change in tastes means less is demanded at every price.

questions.q: Which of these helps to explain why demand curves slope downwards?
options: Firms make more profit at higher prices
At lower prices, the good is cheaper compared with substitutes
Higher prices attract new firms
Costs rise as output rises
questions.why: That is the substitution effect. The other options are about supply.

questions.q: Explain the difference between a movement along a demand curve and a shift of the curve.

ideas.label: A movement is caused by a change in the good's own price
A shift is caused by a change in something other than price, such as income or tastes

questions.model: A movement along the curve is caused by a change in the good's own price, shown as an extension or contraction. A shift is caused by something other than price, such as income or tastes, so more or less is demanded at every price.
questions.why: Own price means movement; anything else means shift.

tests.answer: A movement is caused by a change in the good's own price. A shift is caused by something else like income.
A movement is an extension or a contraction.
They both mean the curve goes to the right.
